record.scope: One run of the automated rehearsal of the first demonstration (scripts/rehearsal, step list version 7) against main in the real application: a production build in headless Chrome over the DevTools protocol, one page per session, a fresh synthetic workspace on acceptance slot 0, and the hosted models through the product's configured client, with main's production derivative worker and its depth model, and the host playing the run's workspace at its shipped pace. In the starter furnished with the small square, the owner chooses an open model for a group of four of its eight people; the world is played and watched walking, a decision that model served is read in the inspector and from the API, someone stands or talks because their model chose it, the square's birds fly and perch on the flight's shared clock while the page's inputs are timed, and the world is paused. The product's compare command then runs a development comparison of that group under two models on one development seed, and the application's Compare view shows it. The person's path runs from uploading synthetic photographs in the drawer through their admission, model rights and review to the depth pass and scene grouping, a world made from them, the Companion asked inside it (a grounded question, an absent place, a change the design refuses and one Customize shows, each answer redrawn after a reload), and the return to it, where one more photograph is added; people are then brought into the made world on its declared floor. The human review is the rehearsal driver's stand-in for a person's review, stated in stand_in_disclosure; no person reviewed these photographs. Each step is a person's action with its declared observable results; each gate of docs/product-direction.md is reported with its first failed step, and a gate that rests on the stand-in never as a plain pass.

The images are the bytes the run captured, and each matches the SHA-256 the run recorded for it. Durations the run wrote in seconds are given here in whole milliseconds.

scene reconstruction: docs/capabilities/scene-reconstruction.md and the scene jobs
steps.reason: What this rehearsal runs, and what it cannot. It runs main's production derivative worker with its depth model (runtime.derivative_worker: MoGe-2 on this machine's CPU), which makes a point map of each reviewed photograph, and the scene grouping that closes each job; wait-for-depth-and-grouping observes both, and a made world draws each photograph from its point map. It does not run multi-view reconstruction. Scene grouping selects a group for pose recovery only when it holds at least three photographs, each with a point map (SceneGroupPosePolicy in exulanica/ingest/scene_selection.py), and the rehearsal's drawings are a day apart, so each is its own group and no scene job exists. The scene worker (exulanica-scene-worker) also requires the pose runtime image by digest as provenance (exulanica/ingest/scene_worker_command.py), and this machine builds no image, so it cannot be started here with a truthful record; Gaussian training needs GPU compute this machine does not have. No control in the application shows a scene's coverage.

what_this_does_not_show: The human review of every photograph was recorded by the rehearsal driver through the drawer's own controls as a stand-in for a person's review; no person inspected these photographs, and every gate resting on it reports passed_on_stand_in or worse, never a plain pass.
The photographs are synthetic drawings in a synthetic workspace; no personal photograph is involved.

The depth pass ran MoGe-2 on this machine's CPU in main's production derivative worker. No multi-view reconstruction ran: no scene group held three photographs, and the scene worker was not started (reconstruct-scene-geometry states why).
The proposed place was confirmed through the identity routes rather than in the application.
Stopping a right in the drawer was not exercised by this run.
One run: the Companion's answers vary between runs.
Access used the production build's operator token gate; account sign-in was not exercised.
No person observed the run and no demonstration footage was recorded; no frame time was judged. The walking measure counts the frames in which drawn walkers moved, over one window of one run.

The living world was watched in the starter at the host's shipped pace with one population of eight; the walking threshold comes from lane W2's two measured arms, not from a pre-registered held-out set.
One group of four was decided by one open model; the people were not split into several groups under different models, and no refused proposal was required to occur.
The comparison ran one development seed, which is never judged, with no same-model control pair; its verdict claims no difference, and one seed says nothing about which model serves people better.
The comparison was started by the product's local command, not from the application.
No client other than the browser read the comparison, its runs or their decisions.
Customize's own refusal of a proposal was not exercised: no request in words produces one.
The birds' measure compares drawn motion with the served flight states; it does not judge how natural the flight looks.
Other work loaded the machine during the run (machine_load, from the GPU slot's own log lines); the times are not timing measurements.
